correctness.rationale: For q>1, epsilon>0, r>0 the positive Helson matrix is B diag(j^-r) B*, B e_j(n)=sqrt(2delta_j)n^(-1/2-delta_j). The Gram kernel is 2sqrt(delta_j delta_k)zeta(1+delta_j+delta_k); subtract the pole 1/(delta_j+delta_k) to obtain sech((j-k)log(q)/2) plus a rapidly decaying remainder. The integral-test bound 0<=zeta(1+t)-1/t<=1 makes the weighted remainder exponentially approximable in finite rank, hence negligible at any polynomial singular-value scale. The Toeplitz symbol f_q has strictly positive Poisson-summed sech representation, and localized banded Toeplitz block asymptotics yield the counting function N(t)~t^-1/r mean(f_q^(1/r)). Monotone inversion and Weyl/Ky-Fan perturbation inequalities give lambda_n~n^-r(mean f_q^(1/r))^r; the p>0 Schatten and logarithmic weak-endpoint conclusions follow by the p-series. In independent bounded calculations 361 exact-form Gram identities matched sech to roundoff, and the Fourier symbol minimum was positive (q=5 sample min~0.03391), mean 1 and second moment 2.4859146897, consistent with Parseval. Finite Fourier computations do not replace spectral counting.
